newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy hard-left confirms support for Prodi govt.
newsitem.headline: Italy hard-left confirms support for Prodi govt.

text.p: Italy's hard left Communist Refoundation affirmed its support for the centre-left government on Friday after a commission in the lower house of parliament voted against the proposed 1997 mini-budget.

"Communist Refoundation repeats its loyalty to the government, confirmed by its vote in favour in the budget commission on the mini-budget," the party's lower house party leader Oliviero Diliberto said in a statement.
"From the result of the vote one can see clearly who are the true enemies of Prodi's government within the coalition."
The commission's office said the vote against the mini-budget was 25 against and 24 for. Two members of the centre-left Olive Tree coalition voted against.
They were identified as Roberto Villetti, from a small socialist party within the coalition, and Giuseppe Bicocchi of the small Segni Pact.
Both were members of the Italian Renewal party group in parliament until last December. Italian Renewal is led by Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini.
The government has a majority in the upper house of parliament but relies on uneasy backing from Refoundation for a majority in the lower house.
